name: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
affiliations: Wroclaw University of Science and Technology
problem: Transformers parallelise during training but are quadratic and memory-hungry at inference; RNNs are linear and constant-memory at inference but do not parallelise during training. Architecture families are usually a choice, not both.
mechanism: RWKV is formulated so the SAME model is a Transformer during training and an RNN during inference: a linear-attention formulation with time-mixing (WKV) and channel-mixing blocks, plus a receptance-gated formulation that lets the recurrence be expressed in a numerically stable closed form with no time-step hyperparameter. Constant memory and constant compute per token at inference.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract): scaled to 14B parameters, 'by far the largest dense RNN ever trained', performing ON PAR with similarly sized Transformers. That is a quality claim, not a speedup: the abstract states constant computational and memory complexity during inference without attaching a multiplier or a baseline engine.

MERGED FIELD BY FIELD - nothing was silently dropped:
  mechanism: the retired record's text was materially fuller (1083 chars vs 384) and is RETAINED here rather than discarded. Its text: Recurrent Weighted Key Value (RWKV) is formulated so the same model computes three ways: as a Transformer (parallel training), as an RNN (constant-cost sequential inference), and as a chunkwise-recurrent hybrid. The layer replaces softmax attention with a data-dependent exponential decay: for the time-mixing sublayer, WKV_t = (sum_i e^{-(t-1-i)w + k_i v_i^T) / (sum_i e^{-(t-1-i)w + k_i}) + D u_t, where w is a learned per-channel decay rate, so the attention weight at distance d is e^{-wd}, a fixed exponential window rather than a learned softmax. The channel-mixing sublayer is a standard position-wise feed-forward with squared ReLU. State is a fixed-size vector per channel of W per token, CONSTANT in sequence length, so there is no KV cache; RWKV was one of the first open architectures to make that concrete for LLMs, and its inference cost is genuinely independent of context length. Version lineage matters: RWKV-4 is the LSTM-style version above, RWKV-5 (Eagle) and RWKV-6 (Finch) change the mixing formulas, and RWKV-7 'Goose' moves to a delta-rule-style state update.
  speedup_reported: the retired record's text was materially fuller (499 chars vs 329) and is RETAINED here rather than discarded. Its text: The paper claims comparable or better performance to Transformers of similar size at 14B scale while being 10x faster at inference, with memory independent of sequence length. Hardware was A100/RTX-class GPUs. Important caveat that survived contact with practice: the '10x faster' figures come from the authors' own kernels and small-batch settings, and the sequential scan has the same fundamental character as Mamba's, so engine support and tuned throughput are much weaker than the paper implies.
